0.x: **Surat (1613)** = the English Company's **first permanent factory in India** – on a **farman of Jahangir**.
**Masulipatnam (1611)** came earlier but only as a temporary trading post (permanent factory 1616): first factory in India = **Surat**; first in South India / Andhra = **Machilipatnam**.

r: Third voyage; landed at **Surat 1608**; at Jahangir's court (Agra) **1609**; first envoy of **James I**; permission withdrawn under Portuguese pressure
**Captain Thomas Best** defeated the **Portuguese** off Surat → Jahangir's farman of **1613** (factory under Thomas Aldworth)
Ambassador of **King James I** to **Jahangir**; no commercial treaty, but privileges for factories at **Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach**; chaplain **Edward Terry**
First Englishman to visit **Akbar's** court (Agra, Fatehpur Sikri)
Seat first at **Surat**, shifted to **Bombay in 1687**
**Factories of the 1st quarter of the 17th century**

0.x: Company formed under **Akbar** (1600); first factory under **Jahangir** (1613, Surat); Roe sent by **James I**.

r: **31 December 1600**, **Queen Elizabeth I** → Company founded in **1600**
"**The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies**"; promoted by the "**Merchant Adventurers**" (1599)

Only **exclusive trading rights** – a **15-year monopoly** between the **Cape of Good Hope** and the **Straits of Magellan** (made indefinite in 1609); **no territorial governance or legislative power**
A **Governor + 24-member committee** (later Court of Directors); shareholders = General Court (later Court of Proprietors)
Under **James Lancaster** (flagship **Red Dragon**, capital £68,000) → factory at **Bantam** (Java)
First chartered to trade with India
"The English Company trading to the East Indies"
Coin money, jurisdiction, **war and peace with non-Christians**
Rival companies merged – **United Company of Merchants of England Trading to the East Indies**
Company rule ended – **Government of India Act, 1858**

1.x: **Early objective:** **eastern trade** (spices, textiles), paid for with **imported bullion**; secret of later success: absence of nationalism and a western-trained army.

r: **Francis Day** (with **Andrew Cogan**), of the Masulipatnam council, got **Madraspatnam** on lease from the **Chandragiri** ruler **Venkatapati Raya III**, through the **Damerla brothers (Venkatadri, Ayyappa)**
At Madraspatnam (near **Mylapore**/San Thome); built from 1 March 1640, completed **23 April 1644** (St George's Day)
**First fort built by the English in India**; **first fortified English settlement**
Chief of the east-coast factories (1641); **presidency 1684**; **first municipality in India (1687-88)**
**Trade in locally woven piece-goods** (Andhra settlements and Fort St. George)
**Madras about 3 lakh**, Calcutta 2 lakh, Bombay 70,000 → **Madras largest**
**Shah Shuja** (subahdar) let the English trade in Bengal for Rs 3,000 a year → **first English factory in Bengal = Hugli (1651)**, then **Qasim Bazar**, Patna, Rajmahal
**Job Charnock**, chief of the **Qasim Bazar** factory, returned to **Sutanuti** → **founder of Calcutta**
Zamindari of **Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata** bought
Fortified settlement named **Fort William** – Sir **Charles Eyre** first president
**Fort William** – Calcutta; Fort St. David – Cuddalore; Fort St. George – Madras

3.x: **Fort St. David:** English fort at **Devanampatnam (Tegnapatnam) near Cuddalore**, bought in **1690**.

r: Bombay came to **Charles II** as dowry of the **Portuguese** princess **Catherine of Braganza** (married 1662)
Charles II gave it to the Company for **£10 a year** (some books give 1674/1688)
**Gerald Aungier** (President of Surat and Governor of Bombay) made Bombay a major commercial hub – "founding father" of Bombay
Bombay **replaced Surat** as the chief English settlement on the west coast

4.x: **Hornby Vellard:** sea wall closing the Worli breach, approved by Governor **William Hornby** (1771-84), completed 1784.

5.x: Order of English centres: **Surat 1613 → Madras 1639 → Bombay 1668 → Calcutta 1690**.

r: Under **Josiah Child** (London) and **Sir John Child** (in India) the Company fought **Aurangzeb**, lost, and was pardoned on paying a fine; Aurangzeb demanded Sir John Child's expulsion
Sacked Surat twice (1664, 1670); threatened the English factory

5.x: **Farman of 1717** (mission of **John Surman**, 1715) by **Farrukhsiyar** = "**Magna Carta**" of the Company.

r: All duties dropped for **Rs 10,000** a year
Company coins current in the Mughal empire

5.x: Misuse of dastaks for private trade drained the Nawab's revenue → Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764) → **Bengal** became the first major territorial base.
